patch_description: Replace the naive ring layout with a hexagonal (triangular) lattice arrangement of 26 sites, which is the densest local arrangement for equal circles and yields near-uniform nearest-neighbor distances. Then, instead of the crude pairwise scaling (which shrinks radii far too aggressively and yields only ~0.96), compute the optimal radii for the fixed centers exactly via linear programming (scipy.optimize.linprog): maximize sum(r_i) subject to r_i + r_j <= d(i,j) for all pairs and r_i <= border distance. This LP is the exact optimum for fixed centers, so any improvement comes purely from better site placement. The hexagonal layers (rows of 5,4,5,4,5,3) fill the square efficiently and place many circles near the boundary where border constraints dominate, which is characteristic of best-known square packings around n=26.
